run.question: My AWS Lambda function 'payment-processor' in us-east-1 has high latency issues. Investigate why.

report.summary: The requested subject could not be observed. The authorized target m0-otel-20260909 is a single-node Kubernetes / OpenTelemetry-demo cluster (node opspilot-m1-control-plane, provider kind://docker/...), not AWS: the deployment inventory contains 24 deployments whose payment-related entry is 'payment' in namespace otel-demo (image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-payment), and no object named 'payment-processor' or containing 'lambda' appears in the deployments, pods, services, configmaps or namespaces I listed. The AWS/CloudWatch metrics that would answer the question (Lambda Duration, InitDuration, ConcurrentExecutions, Errors and the function's log group) are not among the data sources available to this Run, so the runbook lambda-performance-troubleshooting could not be executed: its CloudWatch metric and CloudWatch Logs Insights steps (Steps 1-5) were not carried out because no CloudWatch/CloudWatch Logs integration and no aws CLI surface exist here. The alternative telemetry path also failed: every Prometheus and Jaeger call I made (metric names, label values, series, instant query, range query, target health, trace search, service list) returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no latency series or error-rate reading exists for any service, including the demo's 'payment'. For the different entity otel-demo Deployment payment, the only signals I could read are Kubernetes state and application logs: 1/1 ready, pod payment-6f7bc865d6-wwqnm Running with 0 restarts, and the 60 newest log lines (of 192 read, 16:07:57Z-16:23:06Z) are all info-level 'Charge request received.' / 'Transaction complete.' with no error-level line in that subset. That is not evidence about 'payment-processor' and it is not a latency measurement. No causes of high Lambda latency can be named from this Run; conclusion is inconclusive and no root cause is assigned.

claims.text: The target's deployment inventory holds 24 deployments (ad, cart, checkout, currency, email, flagd, frontend, frontend-proxy, image-provider, jaeger, kube-state-metrics, load-generator, otel-collector, payment, product-catalog, prometheus, prometheus-readonly-proxy, quote, recommendation, shipping, valkey-cart plus coredns, metrics-server, local-path-provisioner); none is named payment-processor or otherwise Lambda-related, and the only payment-related workload is Deployment payment in namespace otel-demo.

Deployment payment in namespace otel-demo shows 1 ready and 1 available replica, and its pod payment-6f7bc865d6-wwqnm is Running with restart count 0, running image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-payment (an OpenTelemetry-demo gRPC payment service, not an AWS Lambda function).

The cluster has a single node opspilot-m1-control-plane whose providerID is kind://docker/opspilot-m1/opspilot-m1-control-plane (kernel 6.8.0-149-generic, linux), i.e. a local kind/docker cluster rather than an AWS/EKS or Lambda runtime environment.

Service inventory in namespace otel-demo (26 Services: ad, alertmanager, alertmanager-headless, cart, checkout, currency, email, flagd, frontend, frontend-proxy, image-provider, jaeger-agent, jaeger-collector, jaeger-query, jaeger-query-nodeport, kube-state-metrics, load-generator, otel-collector, payment, product-catalog, prometheus, prometheus-readonly-proxy, quote, recommendation, shipping, valkey-cart) contains no Service named payment-processor.

For the different entity otel-demo Deployment payment, the 60 newest log lines read from pod payment-6f7bc865d6-wwqnm (60 of 192 lines read, covering 2026-11-23T16:07:57Z to 2026-11-23T16:23:06Z) are all level=info entries 'Charge request received.' and 'Transaction complete.'; no error-level line appears among those shown lines, and no previous container instance exists (no restart).

Against the assumption that the asked-about function exists in this target: the deployment, pod and service inventories of the authorized cluster contain nothing named payment-processor and nothing matching 'lambda' or 'process', so the high-latency report on AWS Lambda function 'payment-processor' in us-east-1 cannot be confirmed, located or measured from this target; the Kubernetes namespace list also contains no AWS-specific namespace (default, kube-node-lease, kube-public, kube-system, local-path-storage, opspilot-readonly, otel-demo).

If the intended subject is the otel-demo 'payment' service rather than an AWS Lambda function, its latency would have to be judged from traces_span_metrics_calls_total / rpc_server_duration_milliseconds_bucket{service_name="payment"} or payment spans in Jaeger; that data could not be retrieved in this Run (all Prometheus and Jaeger calls returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so the demo payment service's latency is unmeasured and no latency problem is established for it.

To answer the original question, connect a CloudWatch/CloudWatch Logs data source and supply, for function payment-processor in us-east-1 over the incident window: Duration (Average/Maximum/p99), InitDuration (cold-start average/count), ConcurrentExecutions (Maximum), Errors/Throttles, memory used vs configured, and the function's log group; then compare against a comparable earlier baseline before calling the latency a regression, and check the function's downstream dependencies (any HTTP/gRPC or DB/SDK client) for their own latency.

gaps: No AWS source is available to this Run: CloudWatch metrics (Duration, InitDuration, ConcurrentExecutions, Errors, Throttles) and CloudWatch Logs for function 'payment-processor' in us-east-1 cannot be queried, and the runbook lambda-performance-troubleshooting steps 1-5 (CloudWatch get-metric-statistics, filter-log-events, Logs Insights memory query) could not be carried out; the missing integration is CloudWatch/CloudWatch Logs plus any aws CLI surface.

'payment-processor' was not found as any Kubernetes object in the authorized target, and us-east-1 / AWS Lambda does not appear anywhere in the target's inventories; the question's subject may therefore not exist in this environment at all.

Every Prometheus call (get_metric_names, get_all_labels, get_label_values, get_series, execute_prometheus_instant_query, metrics_range_query, get_prometheus_target) and every Jaeger call (traces_list_services, traces_search) in this Run returned status error / SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no metric series, error rate, histogram or trace was readable; missing series are unknown, not zero, and latency cannot be quantified for any service, including the demo's payment.

No latency measurement exists for otel-demo Deployment payment: its logs only show info-level charge/transaction messages and Kubernetes state (1/1 ready, 0 restarts); whether it is slow is unknown because traces and rpc_server_duration/rpc_client_duration metrics were unreachable.

No Kubernetes Events were returned for the authorized window (the grouped events query matched nothing, status no_data), so no in-cluster event evidence exists for any workload; this does not prove nothing happened.
Change history is not integrated, so no deployment, configuration or scaling change can be correlated with any latency onset.
Payment pod log reading was limited to the newest 60 of 192 read lines; earlier lines are unknown.
next_steps: Enable/route a CloudWatch (logs + metrics) data source for us-east-1 and re-run the Lambda duration, InitDuration, ConcurrentExecutions and error/throttle queries against the actual incident window.

Confirm whether the intended subject is AWS Lambda 'payment-processor' or the OpenTelemetry-demo 'payment' service; if the latter, restore the Prometheus/Jaeger path (prometheus-readonly-proxy service and jaeger-query) and query traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="payment"} and rpc_server_duration_milliseconds for a comparable baseline window.

If the Lambda exists, collect its configured memory size, timeout, provisioned concurrency, VPC/subnet attachment and its downstream dependency latencies to separate cold-start, concurrency-throttling and dependency causes.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). <none> means the path reached no value in that object, not that the field is absent from the kind; a filtered table is not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
